title: IPv6 ACLs: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: I P version six has its own access lists. They work a little differently. Let's see how.

scenes.heading: The museum guard
scenes.narration: A museum guard checks visitors against a list. I P version six lists are always named, never numbered. You apply one with I P version six traffic filter. For remote access lines, use access class. And some neighbour discovery messages are allowed automatically.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. I P version six lists are always named. The apply command is I P version six traffic filter. And neighbour discovery is allowed by default.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva IPv6 ACLs lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. They are always named. Apply with I P version six traffic filter. Neighbour discovery is permitted by default. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva IPv6 ACLs lab.
